question: What color and dimensional limits apply to crosswalk markings, including transverse crosswalk lines?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Crosswalk markings must be white. Transverse lines, where used, must be between 6 and 24 inches wide (this same 6–24 inch limit applies to the transverse lines that establish a ladder crosswalk). A marked crosswalk must be at least 6 feet wide, increased to a minimum of 8 feet at a non-intersection crosswalk where the posted speed limit is 40 mph or greater. Standards (mandatory): - "Crosswalk markings shall be white. When used, transverse lines shall not be less than 6 inches or greater than 24 inches in width." (Section 3C.03, shown in [Image 2]) - "Except as provided in Paragraph 6 of this Section, the minimum width of a marked crosswalk shall be 6 feet." (Section 3C.03, shown in [Image 2]) - "At a non-intersection crosswalk where the posted speed limit is 40 mph or greater, the minimum width of the crosswalk shall be 8 feet." (Section 3C.03, shown in [Image 2]) - "The transverse lines used to establish the limits of the ladder crosswalk shall not be less than 6 inches or greater than 24 inches in width." - "If paving materials are used to function as the white transverse lines to establish a marked crosswalk, white additives shall be part of the mixture to produce a white surface. The white paving materials shall be retroreflective." (Section 3C.03, shown in [Image 3]) Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 3C-1 shows the dimensional envelopes for each design: transverse lines 6–24 inches wide with a 6 ft minimum crosswalk width; longitudinal bars 12–24 inches wide with 12–60 inch gaps (not exceeding 2.5 times the bar width); ladder crosswalks combining transverse lines (6–24 inches) with longitudinal bars; and bar pairs of 8–12 inch bars separated by a distance d (8 in ≤ d ≤ 12 in), with a footnote that the minimum crosswalk width is 8 feet at non-intersection crosswalks with posted speeds of 40 mph or greater. - [Image 2] Section 3C.03 (Design of Crosswalk Markings) states the white color requirement, the 6–24 inch transverse line width limits, the 6 ft minimum crosswalk width, and the 8 ft minimum at high-speed non-intersection crosswalks, and reproduces Figure 3C-1. - [Image 3] Section 3C.03 continues with the requirement that white paving materials used as transverse lines contain white additives and be retroreflective, and Section 3C.04/3C.05 describe transverse line and high-visibility crosswalk designs. - [Image 4] The table of contents confirms Chapter 3C (Crosswalk Markings) sections, including Section 3C.03 Design of Crosswalk Markings and Section 3C.07 Ladder Crosswalks. - [Image 5] Section 3H.03/3H.04 addresses aesthetic surface treatments for crosswalk interiors, including guidance on contrast gaps adjacent to the white crosswalk lines, but does not alter the white color or dimensional requirements for the crosswalk markings themselves. Citations: - Section 3C.07 Standard §4 (p.592) - Figure 3C-1 (p.590) - Page 631 - Page 632
gold_answer: Crosswalk markings must be white. Where transverse lines are used, each line must be at least 6 inches and no more than 24 inches wide. Except for certain ramp-terminal cases, the marked crosswalk should be at least 6 feet wide.
